vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-cws-publisher
Version: 0.1.1

The skill bundle automates Chrome extension publishing, involving high-risk capabilities such as broad filesystem scanning (inventory_local_extensions.py), headless browser control (generate_marketing_assets.py), and automated interaction with the Chrome Web Store (publish_extension.py). While the logic is aligned with its stated purpose and includes a security scanner (scan_publish_surface.py) to prevent credential leaks, the use of shell execution and browser automation for sensitive developer tasks meets the threshold for a suspicious classification despite the lack of malicious intent.

llm.summary: The skill's code, runtime instructions, and required tools align with its stated purpose (package, audit, and publish Chrome extensions via OpenClaw); nothing requested or installed is disproportionate or unexplained.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (CWS publish + asset generation + leak scan) matches the code and declared binaries: scripts perform inventory, ZIP packaging, asset rendering, leak scanning, and drive OpenClaw browser automation; required binaries (python3, git, gh, clawhub, openclaw, sips) are reasonable for those tasks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions call the bundled scripts that read and write repository files, scan a user-provided search-root for extension manifests and potential secrets, create screenshots via headless Chrome, and drive OpenClaw to interact with the Chrome Web Store dashboard. These actions are expected for the stated purpose, but the scan/inventory steps will examine any paths under the provided search-root (so the user should choose that carefully and review produced snapshots before publishing).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (scripts are bundled and executed directly). No remote downloads or archive extraction are performed by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. Publishing relies on an OpenClaw browser profile (the user supplies the profile, which must already be signed into the Chrome Web Store) and standard CLIs (gh, clawhub) — this is proportionate to the described functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not attempt to modify other skills or global agent configuration. It writes artifacts under the repo's dist/docs paths and temporary Chrome profile dirs only, which is expected for a publish workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: build, scan, and automate Chrome Web Store publishing. Before running it: (1) inspect the bundled scripts and confirm you trust the repo; (2) run only against an explicit --search-root you control (the inventory/scan will examine files under that path); (3) ensure your OpenClaw browser profile is the profile you intend to use and is signed in (the script will save dashboard snapshots under dist/openclaw); (4) note some utilities are macOS-oriented (detects Chrome in macOS app path; uses sips and pkill) — adjust or run on a compatible system; (5) review scan_publish_surface outputs for any leaked tokens before publishing; and (6) don't run this with elevated privileges or against a system-wide root path unless you understand the consequences.
